target_customer: Mobile app and web developers and marketers who send push notifications, email, SMS and in-app messages
problem: Developers needed an easy, scalable way to message app users; the founders built their own tool at their game studio and then offered it to everyone.

founders.name: George Deglin
previous_startups: Hiptic Games (mobile game studio, became GameThrive then OneSignal)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a technical founder and CEO; the OneSignal about page and TechCrunch name only him. A search result says Long Vo co-founded but no opened page does, so he is not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable delivery across APNs, GCM and web push at scale is standard but demanding infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: SDK integrations lock in apps and a free tier drove wide adoption, but delivery APIs are replaceable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Parse shut down after Facebook's 2016 announcement, pushing developers to alternatives; OneSignal stayed independent and kept raising.

market_need_then: In 2015 TechCrunch noted developers disliked existing push tools and OneSignal offered a free, simpler option; the company later reports 1.2 billion devices across 130,000 apps.

branding.name_origin: The company began as Hiptic Games and later GameThrive; the OneSignal name was adopted when it targeted all app developers, but the reason for the name is not stated.
branding.domain_note: Uses onesignal.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: A new logo was announced on the company blog; design not described in opened pages
identity.voice_and_tone: Developer friendly, mission statement about democratizing customer engagement

rebrands.why: Per TechCrunch, to target all app developers and marketers, not just game makers

branding.community_and_virality: No merch or fan community found; wide adoption through a free tier and SDKs.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known to developers as a free push option, but a descriptive name and no evidence of cultural pull beyond developer usage.

pivots.to: GameThrive push notifications for game developers
pivots.why: The studio built its own push tool and found it more valuable than the games
Broaden to all app developers and marketers (TechCrunch)

outcome_analysis: OneSignal began as a game studio that built its own push tool, pivoted to a free push service, rebranded from GameThrive to OneSignal in 2015, and raised Series A to C through 2022 for about $80M. It reports over a million businesses and 10 billion messages daily. It remains independent with no layoffs or exit found, and competes with Airship and Braze.
notes: The $170K earlier seed has no date in TechCrunch. The January 2023 Series C-II with ServiceNow rests on a single database (CB Insights, ZoomInfo repeats it); amount unknown. Competitor list is empty because no source dated near the Summer 2011 batch exists (the push product did not exist then). TechCrunch April 2015, four years later, named Urban Airship, Parse Push, Amazon SNS and Appboy as rivals; recorded here only as later context. Series B and C lead details from aggregators partly conflict (SignalFire vs BAM Elevate on C, TechCrunch states BAM Elevate). Total raised about $80M per TechCrunch at Series C; aggregators say up to $84M. Founding year conflicts (2011 vs 2014).
